evidence.excerpt: Revenue management systems can generate rapid within-day rate changes that expose consumers to stark price anchoring effects. This paper reports two controlled online experiments (n = 410 and n = 385) in which Serbian and Hungarian participants evaluated hotel offers under manipulated sequences of displayed price histories. Experiment 1 tests whether an upward reference price trajectory increases willingness to book relative to a flat or declining sequence, holding the current price constant. Experiment 2 introduces a stated 'algorithm-based pricing' explanation and measures its effect on perceived fairness. Results confirm a significant reference price anchoring effect (Cohen's d = 0.41) but show that algorithm attribution reduces perceived fairness scores by 0.6 points on a 7-point scale. No significant moderation by hotel-booking experience is found. The study has implications for how revenue management systems should communicate price rationale to end consumers.
